title: "The Borrowing Rules Demystified"

# The Borrowing Rules Demystified
Rust's compiler enforces two fundamental rules regarding references at compile time:

1. **At any given time, you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references.**
2. **References must always be valid.**

### Why the Rules Exist

This rule (often summarized as **Aliasing XOR Mutability**) prevents **data races**. A data race occurs when:
- Two or more pointers access the same memory concurrently.
- At least one pointer is writing.
- There is no synchronization.

By disallowing simultaneous reading and writing through multiple aliases, Rust eliminates data races before the code ever compiles.
